old: Emission happens when an electron drops to a lower level: n = 4 to n = 2 releases the energy difference as a photon (hydrogen's 486 nm blue-green line). Upward jumps absorb energy.
new: A photon is given off only when the electron drops (n = 1 to n = 3 is a jump up, so it absorbs light). Among the three drops, the photon energy equals the gap between the levels, and hydrogen’s levels crowd together as n increases: the gap from n = 3 to n = 1 is about 0.89 of the full ionization energy, n = 4 to n = 2 about 0.19, and n = 5 to n = 3 about 0.07. So n = 3 to n = 1 gives the most energetic photon (an ultraviolet line); n = 4 to n = 2 gives hydrogen’s blue-green visible line.
